target_customer: Hospitals, surgery centers and dental offices that sedate patients and need continuous respiration monitoring
problem: Patients under sedation can stop breathing unnoticed, and existing monitors such as pulse oximetry and capnography are indirect or poorly tolerated.
business_model: Medical device sales (wireless respiration patch plus monitoring system) to healthcare facilities; later respiratory data platform

founders.name: Michael Chu
founders.background_notes: YC page: worked in Michelle Khine's lab on soft wearable sensors, over 10 papers, 3 lab patents. Makani's site lists him as CEO; a UCI profile also calls him CEO. One Irvine Business Journal snippet quotes Greg Buchert as chief executive, so leadership may have changed.

founders.name: Michelle Khine
founders.background_notes: YC page: professor of biomedical engineering at UC Irvine and serial entrepreneur; the YC page does not give her education or prior employers.

competitors.name: Respiratory Motion (ExSpiron)
competitors.what: Non-invasive respiratory volume monitor using impedance sensing, FDA cleared 2012
competitors.traction_then: marketed in hospitals; figures not stated

competitors.name: Masimo rainbow Acoustic Monitoring
competitors.what: Neck sensor measuring breathing sounds to derive respiratory rate

technical_complexity.rationale: A wireless wearable sensor producing accurate continuous breathing waveforms requires novel sensor materials from university research and FDA 510(k) clearance, which took until 2025.

defensibility.rationale: Lab patents and an FDA 510(k) clearance (K233953, March 2025) raise the bar, though larger monitoring vendors exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copying or acquisition was found through 2026; the company obtained FDA clearance in March 2025 for adult use and said it was preparing a commercial launch.

market_need_then: Sedation safety monitoring is a known gap; the company cites a market for respiratory monitoring devices (pulse oximetry, capnography, spirometry) and a 2015 press release describes capnography and pulse oximetry as inadequate in studies.

branding.name_origin: Makani is Hawaiian for wind, according to a UC Irvine engineering profile; the link to breathing is implied but not stated by the company.

identity.visual_style: medical device brand; product is called the Makani Respiration Monitor

brand_strength.rationale: Local business press and UC Irvine coverage exist, but the name collides with Google's former Makani energy kite company and there is no community or merch evidence.

outcome_analysis: Makani Science spun out of a UC Irvine lab, raised small early funding, and reached FDA 510(k) clearance for its respiration monitor in March 2025 after joining YC in Summer 2021, a slow timeline typical of medical devices. It remains active with an NIH grant for infant apnea work. Commercial traction is not yet public, so the story is a long regulatory path rather than a fast growth outcome.
notes: Irvine Business Journal snippet (page not opened, fetch was rate limited) reports 3.5M raised to date including a 1.5M bridge; PitchBook lists 1.48M; a Signalbase item cites 10M undated. These conflict and are unverified, so none is recorded as a round. The 550K Koa Accel stage is not stated by the source, so it is marked other. NIH grant is dated from FDA clearance coverage (spring 2025) and amount comes from UC Irvine coverage. Founding year is 2018 per YC and 2019 per UCI.
